suggestions.reason: Both fail this run because it lacks the specific zone convention (audience-naming banners, zone markers), even though it has a sensible conventional structure: a reading guide at the top and a labelled 'configuration reference' appendix at the end. If the goal is the outcome (a reader can tell the human narrative from machine/reference material), say so; if it is the convention, name it explicitly in the assertion. 'Zones labeled' also bundles three conditions (human part labelled, reference part labelled, no interleaving), so split it to show which part a run gets right.

The 60-line yardstick lets this run pass with the diagram at L39, behind a preamble, a reading guide, an overview and six ideas (roughly 1.3 rendered screens down because the PNG is 1710 px wide), while 'Glance first' fails the same ordering. Consider anchoring the check to rendered position, or to the diagram being the first block after the overview.

Any explainer passes this, because there is no verdict to invent, so it does not discriminate here. More telling for this eval: whether inferences are presented as source facts. This run added unstated content (repo contents inferred from names, the day-by-day order, a derived 'Quick triage' row, 'Policy Engine runs strict everywhere except local dev') but labelled most of it; an assertion on unflagged inventions would catch the difference.

The notes are genuinely ambiguous ('3 attempts' vs 'retried 3 times' vs three back-off delays). The assertion fixes one reading, but does not say how a document should handle the ambiguity. This run quoted every figure and raised an explicit open question (L138), a good behaviour no assertion rewards, and a doc that silently chose 'three retries' while listing the same delays would pass equally.

Passing on 'no ERROR lines' hides that check_doc.py warns two link targets may not resolve in Azure DevOps (headings with a comma or colon). One of them, #the-pipeline-stage-by-stage, is in the reading path at L13. Since ADO is a named target viewer, consider treating the fragile-anchor warning as a failure for links in the first screen.

No assertion covers length or proportion for a first-week explainer: this run is about 4,100 words and 305 lines, with a second diagram, a seven-item quick-triage and self-check section, and an Appendix B of eight open questions that sits next to the reference material. An assertion on reading time or on keeping the human flow lean would catch padding.

eval_feedback.overall: Solid on content (all 11 components, all figures, glossary, gotchas and week-one actions are correct) but the formatting-structure assertions (zones, human banner, glance-first, claim headings) are the discriminating ones and this run, written without the skill, fails exactly those four. 'No invented verdict' and 'Diagram portable' are close to trivially satisfied here.
